Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def f(g):
    g=[row[:] for row in g]; n=len(g)
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(n) for c in range(n) if g[r][c]==1]
    p=pts[0]; dr=pc:=None

    r_,c_=p

        if g[r_][c_]==1: break
        g[r_][c_]=2; r_+=dr_[0]; c_+=dc_[0]
    return g

import numpy as np, json
# Demo: 1s at (1,1),(3,3),(5,5). Twos at 7..13 odd. Spacing of 1s =2; twos continue with same spacing starting after last 1.
def f(g):
    o=[r[:] for r in g]; n=len(o)
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(n) for c in range(n) if o[r][c]==1]
    # all ones on the same diagonal? group by diag key
    from collections import defaultdict
    dd=defaultdict(list)
    for r,c in pts: dd[r-c].append((r,c))
    res=[]
    for k,ps in dd.items():
        ps.sort()
        step=(ps[1][0]-ps[0][0]) if len(ps)>1 else 1
        r_=ps[-1][0]+step
        while r_<n:
            res.append((r_,r_-k)); r_+=step
    for r,c in res: o[r][c]=2
    return o
print(f(G['Demo pair 1 input'])==G['Demo pair 1 output'])
print(json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])))
